title: Intune Win32 Application Packaging & Deployment
author_notes: Effort tier: T3 (multi-component within Intune: packaging, detection/requirement/supersedence logic, dependencies, ring assignment).
hook: Package and deploy any Windows app through Intune — reliably, with detection that actually works
problem: Getting a Windows application onto your fleet shouldn't be a coin flip. Done by hand, app deployments fail silently: the installer runs but Intune reports the wrong state, detection rules are guesses, dependencies install out of order, and a bad package lands on everyone at once. This solution gives you the repeatable Win32 packaging method — build the .intunewin, write detection and requirement rules that are correct, model dependencies and supersedence, and assign in rings so a bad build never reaches production.
whats_inside: Solution Overview — the Win32 (.intunewin) app model, how the Intune Management Extension installs and reports, detection vs. requirement rules, dependencies, supersedence, and the ring-based assignment model.

Requirements Guide — every prerequisite (Intune, the Win32 Content Prep Tool, install/uninstall command lines, a reliable detection method, requirement rules, source/distribution hygiene) with how to verify and how to implement each if missing.

Implementation Guide — exact, ordered steps: prepare source and capture the .intunewin, create the Win32 app, set install/uninstall commands, author detection and requirement rules, model dependencies and supersedence, assign in pilot/broad rings, then validate and expand.

5 PowerShell scripts — a packaging/wrapper helper, install-detection validation, a deployment success/failure report across the fleet, safe remediation of failed installs, and a target-ring group builder.
Testing & Troubleshooting Guides with explicit pass/fail gates, plus field-proven Best Practices for the assign-once, repeat-everywhere model.
short: The repeatable way to package and deploy Windows apps through Intune — build the .intunewin, author correct detection/requirement rules, model dependencies and supersedence, and assign in rings. Self-guided, tested, a fraction of consulting cost.
short_plain: The repeatable way to package and deploy Windows apps through Intune — .intunewin packaging, correct detection rules, dependencies, supersedence, ring assignment.
meta_description: Package and deploy Windows apps with Intune: .intunewin creation, detection and requirement rules, dependencies, supersedence, and ring-based assignment. Self-guided, tested steps and scripts.
bottom_line: Windows applications that deploy predictably from Intune — correct detection, ordered dependencies, supersedence handled, and ring assignment so a bad package never reaches production — proven on a pilot before you scale.
